title: Reflection of localized degree bounds and normalized truncations
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Assume $J_X$ is fully faithful. Equip $\mathcal R_X$ with the bounded localized t-structure [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], obtained from the ambient integral one [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]. For every $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$,
$$QK\in\mathcal R_X^{\le m}\iff\mathcal H^r(J_XQK)=0\ (r>m),\qquad QK\in\mathcal R_X^{\ge m}\iff\mathcal H^r(J_XQK)=0\ (r<m).$$
There are natural comparisons $J_X(\tau^{\le m}QK)\cong\tau^{\le m}J_X(QK)$ and $J_X(\tau^{\ge m}QK)\cong\tau^{\ge m}J_X(QK)$ preserving the canonical truncation units, counits and triangles. For every $r$, $J_X(\mathcal H^r(QK))$ is the ordinary sheaf $E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(K)$ in degree zero. Consequently $J_X$ identifies the localized heart with the objects of its essential image concentrated in degree zero. The converse degree bounds require no torsion-free integral cohomology and no levelwise reduction-truncation formula.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14(2), standard cohomology and localized truncations, pp. 61-62

proof.text: Write $J=J_X$ and $F=F_X$. By [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor], $J$ is triangulated and $\mathcal H^r(FL)=E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(L)$ naturally. By [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure], an integral $L\in\mathcal C_X^{\le m}$ has $\mathcal H^r(L)=0$ for $r>m$, so $FL$ has the same upper bound; the corresponding assertion holds for $\ge m$. Every object of $\mathcal R_X^{\le m}$ (respectively $\mathcal R_X^{\ge m}$) is isomorphic to $QL$ with the indicated integral bound, by the essential-image description in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], shifted by $m$. The standard ambient bounds are the cohomology-vanishing conditions of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Applying $J$ to those isomorphisms proves preservation of both bounds, for every $m$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), pp. 60-61, and Proposition 6.8.14(2), p. 62: scalar localization and ordinary cohomology; agent deduction of t-exactness

proof.text: For $Z=QK$, take the canonical rational triangle $\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}Z\xrightarrow{\epsilon_Z}Z\xrightarrow{\eta_Z}\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\ge m+1}Z\to(\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}Z)[1]$ of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1), applied to [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Apply the triangulated $J$ of [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Its end terms have ambient bounds $\le m$ and $\ge m+1$ by step 1. Uniqueness of truncation triangles in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1), now applied to the ambient standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], gives isomorphisms $\alpha_Z:J\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}Z\cong\tau_D^{\le m}JZ$ and $\beta_Z:J\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\ge m+1}Z\cong\tau_D^{\ge m+1}JZ$. They give an isomorphism of the entire triangles with identity on $JZ$, including the connecting arrow and the shift comparison of $J$. In particular $\epsilon^D_{JZ}\alpha_Z=J\epsilon_Z$ and $\beta_ZJ\eta_Z=\eta^D_{JZ}$. Replacing $m$ by $m-1$ gives the requested upper comparison at $m$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i)-(ii), pp. 29-30: adjunction and unique canonical truncation triangle

proof.text: These comparisons are natural for every rational morphism $h:Z\to W$. Indeed, the two maps $J\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}Z\to\tau_D^{\le m}JW$ given by $\alpha_W J(\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}h)$ and $(\tau_D^{\le m}Jh)\alpha_Z$ have the same composite $Jh\,J\epsilon_Z$ with $\epsilon^D_{JW}$. The source has bound $\le m$, so injectivity of the right-adjunction bijection in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) makes them equal. Dually, the two upper comparison maps have equal precomposition with $J\eta_Z$, and the left-adjunction bijection makes them equal. This argument applies directly to $h$ in $\mathcal R_X$, hence also to every fraction $f/\varpi^n$; no presentation of $h$ is chosen. The characterizing equations in step 2 establish preservation of units and counits, and uniqueness of the full truncation triangle establishes compatibility with its connecting map.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i)-(ii), pp. 29-30: functoriality from the two truncation adjunctions

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal H^r(JZ)=0$ for $r>m$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], $JZ\in D^{\le m}$. The identity of $JZ$ is then a universal map from $D^{\le m}$ to $JZ$, so the right-adjunction uniqueness in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) says that $\epsilon^D_{JZ}$ is an isomorphism. Step 2 implies that $J\epsilon_Z$ is an isomorphism. Fullness of the assumed fully faithful $J$ lifts its inverse to a morphism $v:Z\to\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le m}Z$. Applying $J$ to $\epsilon_Zv$ and $v\epsilon_Z$ gives the respective identities; faithfulness makes those composites the identities already in $\mathcal R_X$. Thus $\epsilon_Z$ is invertible. Its source belongs to $\mathcal R_X^{\le m}$, and this class is strictly full [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]; hence $Z\in\mathcal R_X^{\le m}$. Combined with step 1, this proves the first equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29-30; agent inverse-lifting calculation using the assumed full faithfulness

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal H^r(JZ)=0$ for $r<m$. Then $JZ\in D^{\ge m}$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and the identity is a universal map from $JZ$ to $D^{\ge m}$. The left-adjunction uniqueness of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) makes the ambient unit $\eta^D_{JZ}:JZ\to\tau_D^{\ge m}JZ$ invertible. The upper comparison of step 2 therefore makes $J\eta_Z$ invertible. Lift its inverse by fullness of $J$; faithfulness applied to the two inverse equations shows that this lift is inverse to $\eta_Z$ in $\mathcal R_X$. Consequently $Z\cong\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\ge m}Z\in\mathcal R_X^{\ge m}$, using the isomorphism closure in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Together with step 1 this proves the second equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29-30, dual adjunction; agent inverse-lifting calculation

proof.text: Use the convention $H^r_{\mathcal R}(Z)=\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\ge0}\tau_{\mathcal R}^{\le0}(Z[r])$ of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1), viewed as a heart object in degree zero. The natural comparisons of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], with the shift-compatible $Q$, give $H^r_{\mathcal R}(QK)\cong QH^r_{\mathcal C}(K)$. The integral truncations restrict the ambient ones by [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]. For a complex representing $K[r]$, the good truncation formulas of [def-kun-truncations] show that $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}$ is the single sheaf $\ker d^0/\operatorname{im}d^{-1}$ in degree zero, namely $\mathcal H^r(K)$ by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Thus $H^r_{\mathcal C}(K)$ is that ordinary sheaf, and belongs to $\mathcal C_X$. Apply $JQ=F$ and the exact scalar extension on sheaves of [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]: $JH^r_{\mathcal R}(QK)\cong(E_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^r(K))[0]$. The kernel, image and quotient calculation, and all comparison functors, are natural, so this is the asserted natural sheaf identification.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), pp. 60-61, and Proposition 6.8.14(2), p. 62; BBD 1.3.6, p. 31; explicit good-truncation calculation

proof.text: An object is in the localized heart exactly when it lies in both bounds at zero [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Steps 1, 4 and 5 identify this condition with $\mathcal H^r(JZ)=0$ for every $r\ne0$. Every object of the essential image is isomorphic to some $JZ$; the same equivalence shows that one concentrated in degree zero comes from a heart object. Full faithfulness of $J$ restricts to the full subcategories on both sides. Hence $J$ identifies the localized heart with the degree-zero objects of its essential image. All steps used the ambient canonical integral and localized truncations, never a formula involving truncation of finite-level reductions. In particular the reflection argument imposes no torsion-freeness on $\mathcal H^r(K)$.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14(2); agent consequence for the essential image, without invoking essential surjectivity

proof_origin.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3), pp. 60-61, and 6.8.14(2), p. 62, together with BBD Proposition 1.3.3, pp. 29-30, and Theorem 1.3.6, p. 31. Formal deduction from the existing scalar-realization and localized-t-structure statements; full faithfulness is assumed, not re-proved.
